ai.definition: Nuclear fusion reactors are devices that achieve the conditions necessary to sustain a self-heating plasma where nuclei of light atoms fuse together, releasing a significant amount of energy.
ai.howItWorks: Achieves sustained and controlled nuclear fusion by employing advanced techniques such as magnetic confinement (tokamaks) or inertial confinement (lasers), which maintain the high temperatures and pressures required for fusion to occur.
ai.problemSolved: Provides a potential source of nearly limitless clean energy, addressing climate change concerns and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.
ai.manufacturing: Requires highly specialized materials and processes to construct and operate reactors safely and efficiently.
ai.buildProcess: Involves designing the reactor architecture, selecting appropriate materials, setting up plasma confinement systems, and developing robust cooling and safety mechanisms.
ai.costDrivers: High initial capital costs, advanced technology requirements, and ongoing operational expenses such as fuel, maintenance, and decommissioning.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to see significant advancements in the next decade with potential for widespread adoption by mid-century.
ai.regulation: Subject to stringent safety and environmental regulations due to the high-energy nature of fusion reactions.
ai.risks: Technological challenges, high initial costs, potential radiation hazards, and long-term waste management issues.
ai.profitability: Uncertain due to current limited commercial deployment and high operational costs; could become profitable with widespread adoption and technological improvements.
ai.futureDevelopment: Focus on improving efficiency, reducing costs, and addressing safety concerns through ongoing research and development.

glossary.def: A state of matter where electrons are stripped from atoms, creating a charged ionized gas.
A toroidal-shaped device that uses magnetic fields to confine plasma for nuclear fusion experiments.
A method of achieving fusion by compressing a fuel target using high-powered lasers or particle beams.

subsystems.name: Confinement system
subsystems.role: holds the fuel together long enough and densely enough for nuclei to fuse — the defining choice in any design.
parts: magnetic coils (tokamak, stellarator) or inertial drivers (lasers, pulsed power)

subsystems.name: Heating and fuelling system
subsystems.role: raises the fuel to fusion temperature and keeps it supplied.

subsystems.name: Vacuum vessel and first wall
subsystems.role: the chamber that contains the reaction and the first surface the escaping particles hit.

subsystems.name: Blanket and tritium breeding
subsystems.role: absorbs the neutrons, turns their kinetic energy into heat and manufactures new fuel from lithium.

subsystems.name: Exhaust and ash removal
subsystems.role: strips waste heat and helium ash so the reaction does not choke itself.

subsystems.name: Balance of plant
subsystems.role: everything between the reaction and the grid.

buildSteps.title: Pick a confinement route
buildSteps.detail: Magnetic designs (tokamak, stellarator) hold a steady plasma with coils; inertial designs (laser or pulsed-power) implode tiny fuel capsules many times per second. The rest of the plant follows from this choice.

buildSteps.title: Design for tritium
buildSteps.detail: Every surface, seal and maintenance procedure must handle a radioactive hydrogen isotope that diffuses through hot metal; the plant must breed as much as it burns.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the vessel and wall
buildSteps.detail: The vacuum chamber is built in sections, welded to tight tolerances, then lined with armour that can survive neutron bombardment and extreme heat flux.

buildSteps.title: Build the confinement hardware
buildSteps.detail: Hundreds of tonnes of superconducting coil are wound and cased, or a bank of laser or pulsed-power drivers is assembled with precise optics.

buildSteps.title: Install blanket modules
buildSteps.detail: Lithium-bearing modules are fitted inside the vessel, each with coolant channels and connections that must be replaceable by remote handling because the interior becomes radioactive.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and cool down
buildSteps.detail: Magnets are enclosed in a cryostat and taken to a few degrees above absolute zero; diagnostics, heating systems and control software are commissioned.

buildSteps.title: Run with hydrogen, then deuterium
buildSteps.detail: Early campaigns use non-fusing gases to tune control, then deuterium alone, before any tritium is introduced.

buildSteps.title: Burn deuterium–tritium
buildSteps.detail: The real fuel is used, neutrons activate the walls and the blanket begins breeding tritium; this is where materials and fuel-cycle assumptions are tested.

buildSteps.title: Generate electricity
buildSteps.detail: Blanket heat drives a turbine through a conventional power block — a step no fusion device has yet taken.

prerequisites.tech: High-field superconducting magnets or high-repetition drivers
prerequisites.why: strong, affordable coils (including high-temperature superconductors) or fast-repeating laser/pulsed-power systems are what make a compact, continuous reactor conceivable.

prerequisites.tech: Plasma conditions with net energy release
prerequisites.why: laser fusion reached scientific energy gain in 2022; no magnetic device has yet produced more fusion energy than it consumed.
a power plant's wall will take years of neutron damage; no qualified material yet survives a full plant lifetime.
tritium is scarce and radioactive; a reactor must breed, recover and re-inject it with very low losses.
a power plant must run for long stretches without the instabilities that can damage the machine.
activated components must be swapped by robots, which is demonstrated only at small scale.

pathway.milestone: ITER being assembled in France and laser-fusion ignition demonstrated at the National Ignition Facility in 2022
pathway.unlocks: the physics and engineering knowledge base for power-plant-scale designs.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants that demonstrate net electricity and closed tritium breeding
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the fuel cycle and materials work in an integrated machine.

pathway.milestone: demonstration reactors running reliably for long periods
pathway.unlocks: the operating data and supply chain needed to finance commercial units.
firm, low-carbon baseload power — contingent on solving materials, tritium and maintenance.
